title: Ten Hats in a Line
statement: Ten prisoners stand in a line facing forward. Each wears a black or white hat and can see every hat in front of them, but not their own or any behind. Starting from the back, each prisoner in turn calls out "black" or "white", and everyone hears every call. A prisoner who calls their own hat colour is freed. They may agree on a strategy beforehand. What is the largest number of prisoners they can guarantee to free?
insight: The last prisoner spends their call on the parity of black hats they can see. Every later prisoner then knows the parity of the black hats from their own position forward, and can deduce their own colour.
redHerring: Pairing prisoners up (one signals to the next), which guarantees only 5.
hints: The prisoner at the back can never be guaranteed. Why?
Can a single bit from the back prisoner help everyone else?
Let the back prisoner announce the parity of black hats they see. What can the next prisoner work out?
solution:
The back prisoner sees nothing of their own hat and no one has spoken, so no strategy can guarantee them. So at most 9.

For 9: the back prisoner calls "black" if they see an odd number of black hats, "white" otherwise. Prisoner 2 sees the hats in front, compares that parity with the announced one, and deduces their own colour. Each later prisoner knows the announced parity, has heard the colours of everyone between (all calls after the first are correct), and sees the rest, so they also deduce their own. 9 are guaranteed.
